Lody · Apple Watch Smart Stack Live Activity

Design proposal v7 (iPhone-aligned colours, size tiers) for the .small supplemental activity family, adapted from the current iPhone Lock Screen / Dynamic Island implementation in modules/lody-kit/live-activity. Fixture titles and timings come from LiveActivityPreviews.swift. 2026-10-11 · v7 aligns every state with the iPhone Lock Screen colours; v6 is kept as board-v6-dots.html · prepared for review, not implemented.

DESIGN MOCKUP Every card on this board is rendered HTML at real Smart Stack point sizes. None of it is a Simulator or device screenshot. Font is Inter standing in for SF Pro; status symbols are hand-drawn SF Symbol stand-ins. Jellyfish and agent logos are the real app assets.

0 · Today's fallback (why this work)ILLUSTRATION OF SYSTEM DEFAULT · NOT A SCREENSHOT

With no supplementalActivityFamilies, watchOS combines compactLeading + compactTrailing: an agent glyph and a timer, symbol or count. The watch never shows which session it is.

1 · In context — 45 mm Smart StackDESIGN MOCKUP

Actual card scale (1 pt = 1 px) on a 198 × 242 pt 45 mm screen. The card is 184 × 80.5 pt per Apple HIG; the platter and corner radius are drawn by the system.

2 · The states — 45 mm, shown at 2×DESIGN MOCKUP

3 · Data out of date (context.isStale)DESIGN MOCKUP

Same rule as iPhone: the content drops to 70 % opacity, the timer is hidden (it would keep counting on data we no longer trust), the status reads “Disconnected” and the timer slot shows wifi.slash + “4m” since the last sync, the status dot and washes are removed, and the glow drops to the faint level iPhone uses for stale (about a third). The title stays, because that is still true.

4 · Always-On / low luminance (isLuminanceReduced)DESIGN MOCKUP · SYSTEM DIMMING SIMULATED

No large bright fills: the white AgentGlyph square becomes grey, jellyfish glow and washes are removed, status colours darken, and timers switch to minute precision because second-by-second counting is not appropriate when dimmed. The wider “2 min” makes ViewThatFits choose the short status label. The overall darkening shown here is a simulation of what the system applies.

5 · Size matrix — longest fixture titlesDESIGN MOCKUP

Icons and type scale together in three tiers: 45/49 mm (20 pt icon · 13 pt label · 15 pt timer · 15 pt title), 44 mm (19 · 12.5 · 14.5 · 14.5) and 40/41 mm (17 · 12 · 13.5 · 13.5). The status dot and overview rows scale with them. Gaps are measured from the icon edge, cap height and baseline, and are equal within every card. Below 45 mm the status label falls back to “Waiting” / “Done”. One-line titles use the three-equal-gap layout; longer titles take two lines.

6 · Rationale and spec

Design decisions

  • One fixed skeleton, not a scaled Lock Screen card. A 20 pt status row (who · state · time) over the session title. Every state fills the same slots, so the card reads the same way at a glance whichever state it is in.
  • The title is the priority. A title that needs two lines takes both; a one-line title stands alone. No second line is invented: project name, command and question text are not in today's data.
  • A one-line title is not padded. When the title fits on one line, the status row and the title move down together and are distributed with three equal gaps (top, between, bottom), instead of leaving an empty band under the title. On 45 mm that is 16.5 pt each; on 40 mm 13.1 pt.
  • Equal visual spacing. Every card distributes its blocks with equal gaps at the top, middle and bottom, measured from the glyph edge, the first line's cap height and the last line's baseline, not from text frames. Two-line cards: 40 mm 7.4, 41 mm 8.4, 44 mm 9.2, 45 mm 10.5, 49 mm 10.8 pt.
  • One status dot, always a gradient. The dot on the agent icon's bottom-right is the only status mark. Each state uses a two-stop gradient anchored on its iPhone colour, like the running LodyTone.glow: blue→teal (working, pulsing), orange→yellow (waiting), blue→cyan (done), red→pink (failed). The agent icon is never replaced, so the card keeps the same silhouette; the coloured label carries the meaning in words.
  • iPhone first, then balance. Every state uses the Lock Screen's colours and roles: secondary “Working”, orange / blue / red status labels (the pill text colours), primary titles and timers, orange wash for waiting, 16 % blue + 8 % teal wash for completed, no wash for working; the watch adds a red wash for failed (iPhone has none), jellyfish glow in every state. Across states only the label colour, the dot gradient and the wash change; the layout, sizes and weights stay fixed. No green accent.
  • Jellyfish in every state. As on the Lock Screen, every state has the glow, failed and waiting included. On a 184 pt card the 120 pt glow would cover the text, so it is an 84 pt glow cropped at the bottom-right at 30 % opacity (about 11 % when stale, mirroring iPhone's 0.42 → 0.15). The jelly mark identifies Lody in the overview.
  • No invented interaction. No approve, deny or answer buttons. The same .small layout is also used in CarPlay, where Apple advises against controls. Tapping keeps the system behaviour (full screen with Open on iPhone).
  • Simultaneous sessions under attention. While a session waits for you, the iPhone's “1 running” hint is dropped on the watch to protect the title; the overview returns once nothing needs you.
  • Alerts. When an update carries an AlertConfiguration, the watch shows this same card with a haptic, so the waiting layout has to work on its own.

Implementation notes (for the later step, not done now)

Family.supplementalActivityFamilies([.small]) on the existing ActivityConfiguration; branch on @Environment(\.activityFamily) in the content closure. No watchOS app.
SpacingHorizontal 9–10 pt (8–9 on 40–41 mm). Vertically, the 20 pt status row and the text block are spaced evenly (top = middle = bottom), with the text block trimmed to cap height / baseline: in SwiftUI, offset by the font's ascender − capHeight and descender, or align with .firstTextBaseline guides. Two-line block: ~10.5 pt per gap on 45 mm, 7.4 pt on 40 mm. One-line title: ~16.5 pt on 45 mm, 13.1 pt on 40 mm.
TypeThree tiers (45/49 · 44 · 40/41 mm): title 15 / 14.5 / 13.5 pt semibold · status 13 / 12.5 / 12 pt semibold · timer 15 / 14.5 / 13.5 pt rounded semibold monospaced, primary · overview rows 13 / 12.5 / 12 pt, primary · ViewThatFits between “1-line title” and “2-line title”.
GlyphsAgentGlyph / JellyMark 20 / 19 / 17 pt; rows 14 / 13.5 / 12.5 pt. Status dot 7 / 6.5 / 6 pt in a ring of the card colour at the icon's bottom-right, filled with a per-state LinearGradient; only running pulses.
JellyNew 84 pt asset rendition at 1×/2× (ActivityKit greys out images larger than their frame).
DataOnly existing payload fields: title, status, agentLogoKind/Text, timestamps. The catalog gives a session only status (requestPermission / waiting) and awaitingUserSince; whether it is a question or a permission, and the command, live only in the session transcript, which the Live Activity sync does not read. So approval and question share “Waiting for you” (native.liveActivity.status.attention).
StaleExisting lodyStale + staleLabel/lastSyncLabel; no timer.
AODisLuminanceReduced: grey AgentGlyph fill, no glow or wash, minute-precision elapsed text. Check timer behaviour on device.
CopyStatus row uses ViewThatFits: “Waiting for you” / “Completed” on 45–49 mm, “Waiting” / “Done” when narrower; these short forms need localized strings in Copy.
VerifyXcode previews for .small per state, plus watchOS 27 Simulator Smart Stack screenshots compared against this board.
